13:53 Local Time, 11:53 GMT, 17:23 IST: Another delay with the rain making a reappearance. It's a reasonably heavy shower and the players have to rush off. Some respite for South Africa who were being put under severe scrutiny by Boland. He just looks unplayable whenever there's any movement on offer. Easily the most dangerous Australian bowler on show in the little cricket we've seen so far.
14:26 Local Time, 12:26 GMT, 17:56 IST: Rain has reduced but hasn't stopped completely. No movement from the groundstaff as the covers remain in place.

STAT: Swing (3.3 times) and seam movement (1.4 times) have both been lower today than in the opening 12 overs of Day 1 in Durban. Scott Boland has found the least swing but the most seam movement among Australia’s three quicks (2+ overs) so far today.

14:52 Local Time, 12:52 GMT, 18:22 IST: What's the latest? Well, nothing encouraging. The drizzle continues, and the covers remain firmly in place. Tea is scheduled for 15:40, around 50 minutes from now, and it is looking increasingly unlikely that we will see any more play in this session.
15:08 Local Time, 13:08 GMT, 18:38 IST: Tea has been taken early.
15:34 Local Time, 13:34 GMT, 19:04 IST: The rain has set in and the chances of any further play today aren't looking very good.
16:07 Local Time, 14:07 GMT, 19:37 IST: No change in the weather. It's gloomy and wet, and most of the spectators have left.

Day 2, 09:15 Local Time, 07:15 GMT, 12:45 IST: Hello and welcome to what was supposed to be an early start on Day 2. But this is the update from Telford who is at the venue: "Rain fell for much of the night and again this morning. Currently it’s not raining, but everything is wet, wet, wet. Play was to resume 15 minutes early at 9.45am, but that doesn’t seem likely."
Live pictures coming in show that the covers are on and it's raining.
